title: Buttermilk Pie
finish: Custard set, nutmeg, a little tang
summary: Buttermilk, sugar, nutmeg. The Texas custard pie when pecans are expensive and chess already happened.
story: Buttermilk pie is chess pie's cousin who went to the dairy. Tang from the buttermilk, a little nutmeg, a filling that slices. It is what meat-market country cooks when fruit isn't in. Serve at room temp. A berry on the plate is allowed. A sauce is not.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.body: Sugar and flour. Butter, eggs, buttermilk, vanilla, nutmeg, salt. Smooth, not foamy.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: Pour into the crust. 350°F 45–55 minutes until the center is just set. Tent the crust if it darkens.

steps.title: Cool
steps.body: Cool completely. Room temp or cold. Nutmeg on the slice if you like people asking what it is.

proTips.text: Real buttermilk. The leftover from making butter, or the cultured carton. Not milk plus vinegar if you can help it — this pie is named after the dairy.

milestones.label: Filling smooth
milestones.hint: Buttermilk, nutmeg, melted butter.

milestones.label: Just set
milestones.hint: Cool all the way before you slice.

title: Mississippi Mud Cake
finish: Marshmallow layer melted, chocolate frosting set, pecans
summary: Dense cocoa cake, a blanket of marshmallows, chocolate frosting. The Delta pan that looks like river mud on purpose.
story: Mud cake is not a brownie and it is not a sheet cake. You bake a dark cocoa slab, dump marshmallows on the hot cake so they slump, then frost. Pecans. It should be messy to cut. That is the name. Serve from the pan at a pig pickin' and do not apologize for the marshmallows.

steps.title: Batter
steps.body: 350°F. Grease a 9×13. Melt butter with cocoa. Beat in sugar, eggs, flour, salt, vanilla, pecans. Spread.

steps.title: Bake and blanket
steps.body: 30–35 minutes. Pull it, immediately cover with marshmallows, return 2–3 minutes until they slump. Don't let them brown hard.

steps.title: Frost
steps.body: Melt butter, cocoa, milk. Off heat, powdered sugar, vanilla. Pour over the marshmallows. Cool until you can cut squares that still look like mud.

proTips.text: If the marshmallows disappear you waited too long to frost and they dissolved. Frost while they're a melted blanket, not a puddle.

milestones.label: Cake baked
milestones.hint: 30–35 minutes. Pecans in the batter.

milestones.label: Marshmallow blanket
milestones.hint: Slump, then chocolate frosting.

title: Coconut Layer Cake
finish: White crumb, frosting like a cloud, coconut stuck all over
summary: White cake, seven-minute or cream-cheese frosting, a blizzard of coconut. The Sunday cake of the Deep South.
story: A coconut cake is a commitment. White layers, fluffy frosting, coconut pressed into every vertical inch so it looks like a snowball that can feed twelve. Fresh coconut if you are showing off. Bagged sweetened if you are feeding a pit crew after church. Either is Southern. Dry cake is a sin — buttermilk in the batter.

steps.title: Layers
steps.body: 350°F. Grease three 8-inch pans. Whisk flour, baking powder, salt. Cream butter and sugar. Eggs one at a time. Alternate dry and buttermilk. Vanilla. Divide, bake 22–28 minutes. Cool completely.

steps.title: Frost
steps.body: Beat cream cheese and butter. Powdered sugar, vanilla. Stack with frosting between.

steps.title: Blizzard
steps.body: Frost the outside. Press coconut onto the sides and top until you cannot see frosting. Fridge 30 minutes to set. Serve cool.

proTips.text: Toast half the coconut if you want a little nuttiness. All toasted and you lost the snowball. Mix, or keep it white.

milestones.label: Layers cool
milestones.hint: White crumb. Completely cool.

milestones.label: Coconut blizzard
milestones.hint: Press it on. No bald frosting.

title: Biscuit Strawberry Shortcake
finish: Biscuits split, berries juicy, cream not sweet enough to hide the fruit
summary: Buttermilk biscuits, macerated strawberries, barely sweet cream. Shortcake the Southern way — not a sponge cup from the store.
story: Shortcake is a biscuit. If it is a yellow sponge disc from a plastic sleeve you are in a different country. Sugar the berries until they make a syrup. Split a hot biscuit. Cream you whipped yourself. This is June in the Carolinas and it also works with frozen berries in January if you tell the truth about it.

steps.title: Berries
steps.body: Toss strawberries with sugar and lemon. Rest 30 minutes until there is syrup in the bowl.

steps.title: Biscuits
steps.body: 425°F. Flour, sugar, baking powder, salt. Cut in butter. Buttermilk until shaggy. Pat 1-inch thick, cut 8 biscuits. Bake 14–16 minutes until tall and brown.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Whip cream, sugar, vanilla to soft peaks. Split biscuits warm. Berries, cream, biscuit lid, more berries. Serve immediately.

proTips.text: Soft peaks on the cream. Stiff cream is frosting and it fights the berry. You want it to slump into the biscuit.

milestones.label: Berries juicy
milestones.hint: Sugar, 30 minutes, syrup in the bowl.

milestones.label: Biscuits brown
milestones.hint: Hot split. Cream, berries, eat now.

title: Fried Peach Pies
finish: Blistered crust, filling hot, sugar stuck to the face
summary: Hand pies, dried or fresh peach filling, a quick fry. The gas-station legend you can make after the ribs come off.
story: Fried pies are the South's pocket dessert. Dried peaches simmered to a jam, or fresh peaches cooked down, folded in a biscuit or pie-dough half-moon, crimped, fried. Dust sugar. They should leak a little. That is how you know. Apple is legal. Peach is the one people remember from a Tennessee counter.

items: 3 cups chopped peaches (fresh, or 8 oz dried peaches simmered in water until soft)
½ cup cold unsalted butter, cubed
½ cup cold buttermilk, plus a splash
Neutral oil for frying, 2 inches in a Dutch oven

steps.title: Filling
steps.body: Cook peaches, sugar, lemon, cinnamon, salt until jammy, 10–15 minutes. Stir in cornstarch. Cool completely — hot filling explodes in oil.

steps.title: Dough
steps.body: Flour, salt, sugar, butter to peas. Buttermilk until it just comes together. Rest 20 minutes. Roll thin, cut 5-inch rounds.

steps.title: Fry
steps.body: 2 Tbsp filling per round, fold, crimp with a fork. 350°F oil 2–3 minutes a side until blistered gold. Drain. Sugar while hot. Cool 5 minutes or you'll invent a new kind of injury.

proTips.text: Cool filling. Warm filling in a sealed pie is a steam bomb. I have the shirt stains to prove it.

milestones.label: Filling cold
milestones.hint: Jammy peaches. Completely cool.

milestones.label: Crimped
milestones.hint: Fork edges. No leaks until they fry.

milestones.label: Blistered gold
milestones.hint: Sugar while hot. Wait 5 to eat.

title: Bananas Foster
pitTemp: Skillet on the stove (or a side burner)
finish: Bananas caramelized, sauce rum-hot, ice cream melting
summary: Butter, brown sugar, banana, rum. The Brennan's-born skillet you can finish on a pit side burner in five minutes.
story: Bananas Foster is New Orleans tableside theater that also works in a backyard. Butter and brown sugar go to caramel, bananas warm through, rum in, flame if you want the show, cinnamon. Ice cream in the bowl first so the sauce hits cold. This is the 15-minute closer when the cobbler didn't happen.

steps.title: Caramel
steps.body: Skillet over medium. Butter, brown sugar, cinnamon until bubbling and smooth, 2 minutes.

steps.title: Bananas
steps.body: Bananas cut-side down 1 minute, flip 1 minute. They should be warm and coated, not mush.

steps.title: Rum
steps.body: Off heat or on low: rum, vanilla. If you flame it, tip the pan to the gas or a long lighter — keep hair and eaves away. Spoon over ice cream immediately.

proTips.text: Ripe bananas with a few spots. Green ones stay starchy. Black ones dissolve. Spotty is the same rule as pudding.

milestones.label: Caramel bubbling
milestones.hint: Butter, brown sugar, cinnamon.

milestones.label: Sauce on ice cream
milestones.hint: Rum in. Don't wait. It waits for nobody.

title: Pecan Pralines
finish: Set but creamy, pecans in every round, not rock candy
summary: Sugar, cream, butter, pecans. The New Orleans candy that should snap-then-melt, not break a tooth.
story: A praline is not a brittle. Cream and butter keep it fudgy. You cook to soft-ball, stir in vanilla and pecans, drop spoons on wax paper before it sets in the pot. If it sugars up grainy you rushed the dissolve or you scraped the sides like a maniac. Make them the day of. Humidity is the enemy. A tin next to the coffee is the whole presentation.

steps.title: Dissolve
steps.body: Sugar, brown sugar, cream, butter, salt in a heavy pot. Medium heat, stir until the sugar dissolves and it looks smooth. Stop scraping the walls.

steps.title: Soft ball
steps.body: Cook without stirring to 240°F on a candy thermometer, 6–10 minutes. Off heat: vanilla, pecans. Stir until it just starts to thicken and look matte, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Drop
steps.body: Spoon onto wax paper in 3-inch rounds. Work fast. Cool 30 minutes until set. Tin with wax paper between layers. A few days if the weather is dry.

proTips.text: If they turn to sand you crystallized the sugar. Next batch: a lid on the pot for 2 minutes after it boils so the steam washes the walls, then cook to temp.

milestones.label: 240°F
milestones.hint: Soft ball. Pecans and vanilla off heat.

milestones.label: Dropped
milestones.hint: Wax paper. Don't wait for the pot to seize.

title: German Chocolate Cake
finish: Coconut-pecan frosting thick between layers, chocolate crumb
summary: Mild chocolate layers, coconut-pecan frosting cooked on the stove. A Dallas cake, despite the name.
story: German's chocolate was a baking bar. A Dallas newspaper printed a cake in 1957 and Texas never put it down. The frosting is the point: evaporated milk, egg yolk, coconut, pecans, cooked until it spreads like jam. You can leave the sides naked. That is traditional and it looks like you meant it.

steps.title: Chocolate
steps.body: Pour boiling water over the chocolate. Stir smooth. Cool.

steps.title: Layers
steps.body: 350°F. Grease three 8-inch pans. Cream butter and sugar. Yolks, vanilla, chocolate. Alternate flour (with soda, salt) and buttermilk. Fold stiff egg whites. Bake 25–30 minutes. Cool.

steps.title: Frosting
steps.body: Cook evaporated milk, sugar, yolks, butter over medium, stirring, until thick, 10–12 minutes. Off heat: vanilla, coconut, pecans. Cool until spreadable. Stack, frosting between and on top. Sides optional.

proTips.text: The frosting has to cool. Spread it hot and the layers slide like tectonic plates. Wait until it mounds on a spoon.

milestones.label: Layers cool
milestones.hint: Chocolate, buttermilk, folded whites.

milestones.label: Frosting thick
milestones.hint: Coconut and pecan. Stack. Naked sides are honest.

title: Pig Pickin' Cake
finish: Yellow crumb, fluffy pineapple frosting, mandarin on top
summary: Mandarin orange cake, pineapple-whipped frosting. The Carolina whole-hog dessert that is not banana pudding for once.
story: You pick the pig, then you pick this cake. Yellow cake mix is how a lot of firehouses make it — from-scratch yellow batter is how we write it. Mandarin oranges in the cake, crushed pineapple cooked into a pudding frosting with whipped topping folded in. It is light after a grease-heavy plate. That is why it exists.

items: 1 (11 oz) can mandarin oranges, undrained, lightly crushed
1 (8 oz) tub whipped topping, thawed, or 2 cups whipped cream

steps.title: Batter
steps.body: 350°F. Grease a 9×13 or two 9-inch pans. Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, salt. Add oil, eggs, mandarins with juice, vanilla. Beat 2 minutes. Bake 30–35 minutes (9×13) or 22–26 (layers). Cool completely.

steps.title: Frosting
steps.body: Stir pineapple with juice into dry pudding until thick. Fold whipped topping. Spread. Fridge 1 hour. Mandarin slices on top if you still have some.

proTips.text: Keep it cold. This frosting is a pudding. A hot pit tent will turn it into soup. Last thing on the table, first thing back to the cooler.

milestones.label: Cake cool
milestones.hint: Mandarins in the batter. Completely cool.

milestones.label: Pineapple frosting
milestones.hint: Fridge an hour. Serve cold.

title: Kentucky Chocolate-Pecan Pie
finish: Set chocolate custard, pecans toasted, bourbon in the nose
summary: Pecan pie with chocolate and bourbon. The Kentucky Derby weekend pie — not the trademarked bakery one, the home one.
story: Chocolate and pecans and a little bourbon is what Kentucky puts in a pie shell when the horses are running. It is not the packaged 'Derby' pie from Louisville — that's someone else's name. This is the church-cookbook version: dark chocolate, pecans, bourbon, a custard that slices. Serve barely warm. Whipped cream, not a scoop of ice cream fighting the chocolate.

steps.body: Scatter chocolate in the cold crust. It will melt into the custard in the oven.
steps.title: Chocolate

steps.body: Whisk eggs, sugar, corn syrup, butter, bourbon, vanilla, salt. Pecans. Pour over the chocolate.
steps.title: Custard

steps.body: 350°F 45–55 minutes until the center is just set. Cool at least 2 hours. Bourbon whipped cream if you are among friends.
steps.title: Bake

proTips.text: The bourbon should be a hello, not a bar fight. Two tablespoons. More and it tastes like you spilled the bottle.

milestones.hint: Chocolate in the crust, pecans in the custard.
milestones.label: Filled

milestones.hint: Cool 2 hours. Slice clean.
milestones.label: Just set

title: Copycat Kern's Derby Pie
finish: Set at the edge, a little wobble in the center, walnuts and chips in every slice
summary: A copycat of Kern's Derby Pie — chocolate chips and walnuts in a flaky crust. Home kitchen, not the bakery box.
story: This is a copycat of Kern's Derby Pie: chocolate chips, chopped walnuts, butter, sugar, eggs, and a little flour so the filling sets like a warm cookie. Bourbon if you want it. Cool it before you cut. Whipped cream on the side. It is a home version of the Louisville classic — not the pie from the bakery.

items: 1 stick (8 Tbsp) unsalted butter, melted and cooled 5 minutes

steps.body:
325°F. Put the unbaked crust in a 9-inch pie plate. Crimp the edge.
Set the plate on a sheet pan so if it bubbles over you are not scrubbing the oven.
steps.title: Heat the oven

steps.body:
In a bowl, whisk the melted butter and sugar until it looks like wet sand.
Whisk in the eggs, one at a time, then vanilla and bourbon if you are using it.
Stir in the flour and salt until no dry streaks.
Fold in the chocolate chips and walnuts.
steps.title: Mix the filling

steps.body:
Pour the filling into the crust. Spread the chips and walnuts so they aren't all in one pile.
Don't overfill — leave a little rim.
steps.title: Fill the crust

steps.body:
325°F for 45–55 minutes.
Done when the edge is set and the center still has a slight jiggle, like gelatin, not soup.
If the crust browns too fast, tent the edge with foil.
steps.title: Bake

steps.body:
Cool at least 2 hours on a rack. Overnight in the fridge slices cleaner.
Serve at room temp or barely warm. Whipped cream. Not ice cream — this pie is already rich.
steps.title: Cool, then slice

proTips.text: Walnuts. Not pecans. That's the whole point of this pie. If you swap pecans you made the other Kentucky pie already in this app.
This is a home pie. If you are selling pies, don't print the bakery's trademark on a box.

milestones.hint: Butter, sugar, eggs, flour. Chips and walnuts folded in.
milestones.label: Filling mixed

milestones.hint: 325°F, 45–55 min. Slight jiggle in the center.
milestones.label: Just set

milestones.hint: Then slice. Whipped cream.
milestones.label: Cooled 2 hours

title: Texas Twinkies
pitTemp: 225–250°F, then a hot grate to crisp
finish: Bacon crisp, pepper collapsed, glaze set
summary: Jumbo jalapeños stuffed with leftover brisket and cream cheese, wrapped in thick bacon, smoked, then glazed. Hutchins BBQ's leftover-brisket accident.
story: Hutchins BBQ in McKinney started stuffing leftover fatty brisket and cream cheese into the biggest jalapeños they could find, wrapping them in thick bacon, and sending them back through the smoker. A Texas Twinkie is not a halved popper with a smear of cheese. It is a whole pepper, close to a quarter pound of brisket in each one, smoked until the pepper slumps and the bacon renders, then glazed and kissed on a hot grate. Two of them is lunch. Use leftover packer — the point is better than the flat.

items: 8 jumbo jalapeños, 4–5 inches — the biggest you can find
Ice water, optional pinch of sugar in the bath
1 lb leftover smoked brisket, preferably point, chopped small
Kosher salt and coarse black pepper
½ cup sweet Texas-style barbecue sauce

steps.body: Gloves on. Cut a T into each pepper: a slit down one long side and a short cut under the stem, without cutting through. Open it like a book. Scrape out seeds and white pith. Keep the stem. Soak in ice water 15–20 minutes if you want them milder — a pinch of sugar in the bath helps. Drain and pat dry.
steps.title: T-cut and seed

steps.body: Cream cheese in the bottom third of each pepper. Pack chopped brisket on top until the pepper is full and just barely closes. About 2 ounces of each per jumbo pepper. Do not mash brisket and cheese into one paste — you want a bite of bark and a bite of cheese.
steps.title: Stuff 50/50, don't stir it into mush

steps.body: Thin bacon tears and shrinks off. Wrap each pepper with two thick slices so the seam is covered. Toothpick the ends. Dust with salt and coarse pepper like a little brisket.
steps.title: Two slices of thick bacon

steps.body: 225–250°F, post oak. Directly on the grate, 2–2½ hours. Flip once if one side is pale. The pepper should be soft and the bacon rendered but not yet shatter-crisp. Internal around 145°F is fine — everything in there is already cooked except the bacon.
steps.title: Smoke low

steps.body: Brush a thin coat of sweet sauce. Move to a hotter grate or skillet, 350°F-ish, 2–4 minutes until the bacon tightens and the glaze tackifies. Rest 5–10 minutes. Pull the toothpicks. Serve hot.
steps.title: Glaze and crisp

proTips.text: The pepper has to be huge. Grocery jalapeños the size of a thumb make sad little poppers. Mexican markets and the ugly bin are where the rib-sized ones live.
Point meat, not leftover flat. Dry flat plus cream cheese is a brick. Fat is the point of the Twinkie.
Sauce at the end. If you mop it on at 225°F for two hours you steam the bacon and burn the sugar. Smoke first, glaze last, then heat.

milestones.hint: Cream cheese down, brisket packed, two slices thick bacon.
milestones.label: Stuffed and wrapped

milestones.hint: 2–2½ hours at 225–250°F. Pepper soft, bacon rendered.
milestones.label: Smoked

milestones.hint: Sauce, then a hot grate. Rest 5 minutes. Pull the picks.
milestones.label: Glazed and crisp
